extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing an application for the NIH Director's Pioneer Award (DP1) / prospective applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an application to the NIH Director's Pioneer Award (DP1), emphasizing eligibility, application format, required documents, review criteria, and award administration. Targeted to investigators proposing highly innovative, high-impact, high-risk research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on innovation and potential impact over preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: The application’s project description is highly abbreviated to focus on innovation and potential impact rather than preliminary data and experimental details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a concise, innovation-driven essay (5 pages) that emphasizes bold, high-impact ideas and potential significance; avoid long sections of preliminary data or detailed experimental plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant’s potential to make seminal contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Review emphasizes the individual’s potential to make seminal contributions toward solving an important research problem relevant to the broad mission of NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate a track record and evidence of creativity, major contributions, and capacity to shift fields; letters of reference should address this potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project innovativeness and departure from ongoing research
rubrics_metrics.description: Review considers the innovativeness, significance, and potential impact of the project and whether it represents a significant departure from the applicant’s ongoing research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed work is not an obvious extension of current or prior work; articulate fundamentally new insights or radically unconventional hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'new research direction'
rubrics_metrics.description: A new research direction is distinct from any research currently or previously conducted by the applicant or by other investigators; it cannot simply be an obvious extension or scaling up of a research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence that the idea stems from a fundamentally new insight or exceptionally innovative approach rather than incremental extension; clarify how this differs from past work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of applicants at all career stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals at all career stages are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although eligible, early-stage/postdoctoral applicants must show concrete evidence of innovativeness and independence; institutional policies may limit eligibility administratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign scientist eligibility and institutional requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-U.S. citizens may apply, but PIs must hold an independent position at a U.S. institution that is eligible to apply. Non-domestic (foreign) organizations are not eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the PI’s appointment is at an eligible U.S. institution; foreign institutions cannot be the applicant organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH intramural scientists ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists in the NIH Intramural Research Program (IRP) are not eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit an application if you are an NIH intramural scientist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Principal Investigator only
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a single investigator is allowed on the application (multiple Principal Director/Principal Investigators are not accepted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborators and consultants are allowed and may be funded, but do not list co-PIs or multiple PD/PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborator/consultant inclusion restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators may be included and described in the Research Strategy essay, but collaborators may not be listed as Senior/Key Personnel, their Biographical Sketches cannot be included, and Letters of Support are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List names/affiliations of collaborators in the PHS Assignment Request Form so NIH staff can exclude them as reviewers; do not include biosketches or letters for collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time/effort commitment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients are expected to devote the major portion (at least 51%) of their research time/effort to activities supported by the Pioneer Award in the first three years; minimum of 4 person-months (33%) in year 4, and 3 person-months (25%) in year 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar months are used; effort percentages apply to total research time only (exclude teaching, clinical, administrative duties). Do not apply if you cannot meet these commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on expanding ongoing projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pioneer Award is meant to support a distinctly new research direction. Proposals should not enable investigators to expand ongoing research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly justify how the proposal is a departure from the investigator’s existing program rather than an expansion or continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on PI serving on multiple Pioneer applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An investigator may serve as the PI on only one application in response to the funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit more than one Pioneer application as PI for the same FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH expects to make approximately seven awards; recent success rate (FY2020–2024) is 4%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize high competitiveness and limited number of awards when framing scope and innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Letter of Intent (LOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of intent are not required or accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prepare or submit an LOI for this FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission deadlines and late policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be received by Grants.gov no later than 5:00 p.m. local time on the due date; late applications will not be accepted and no extensions provided for peer review service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan institutional registrations and submission well ahead of deadlines; letters of reference must be submitted by referees by the same due date (5:00 p.m. local time of the referee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required institutional registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution must be registered with Grants.gov and System for Award Management; both institution and investigator must register in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start registrations early (may take up to six weeks); work with your AOR/Sponsored Research Office to confirm institutional processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document format and page limit compliance (PDF and page limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents must be in PDF format and cannot exceed page limits. Specific formatting instructions are in the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceeding page limits may render an application non-responsive and not reviewed; follow SF424 instructions closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5-page essay replaces Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The 5-page essay replaces the traditional Research Plan; requirements differ from other NIH grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey significance, innovation, and potential impact concisely within five pages; include effort commitment statement in the Research Strategy essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations, figures, and no separate bibliography page
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations and references are allowed within the 5-page essay as long as they fit; a separate 'Bibliography & References Cited' page is not allowed. Figures and illustrations are allowed if they fit within five pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any essential citations/figures inside the five pages; do not rely on reviewers to follow external links—applications must be self-contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: No movies or URLs for essential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Movies, links to websites, or CDs are not allowed; internet URLs may not be used to provide information necessary to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include web links to replace critical content; if a cited publication includes a movie online, list it as a citation but include all critical information in the essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix and post-submission data restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only limited Appendix materials are allowed per SF424 Guide; no additional documents beyond allowed sections; new data after submission are not accepted except for unforeseen events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Appendix instructions strictly; additional materials may cause the application to be excluded from review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget format and fixed total direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed budgets are not required or accepted. Applicants are instructed to enter $3,500,000 total direct costs for the 5-year project period (annual increments of $700,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit a line-item budget. Indirect costs will be determined at award time and are in addition to direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project period requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are instructed to request a project period of five years; scope should be commensurate with this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design aims consistent with a five-year timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants planning research that results in the generation of scientific data are required to comply with instructions for the DMS Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include DMS Plan within the 'Other Plan(s)' field on the PHS 398 Research Plan Form; samples and guidance available on DMS website. GDS plans do not substitute for DMS Plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional funds for Data Sharing and Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not request additional funds for Data Sharing and Management; the budget should be flexible enough to manage data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not add a separate budget line for DMS activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign component and foreign subaward policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign components are allowed but must abide by NIH policy. NIH is establishing policies that will prohibit foreign subawards from being nested under the parent grant and is developing tracking systems; until ready NIH will not issue awards that include a subaward to a foreign entity that would receive funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between foreign components (may be allowable) and foreign subawards (subject to restrictions); follow current NIH policy and provide required justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to declare foreign collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project includes a collaboration with an investigator at a foreign institution (even if no funds are exchanged), the applicant must mark 'Yes' on item #6 of the R&R Form and include a foreign justification document, or risk administrative withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively prepare and include foreign justification documentation when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirement and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must arrange for three (and no more than three) letters of reference to be submitted on their behalf via eRA Commons by the application due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each letter must be from one individual; applicants will receive e-mail confirmations when letters are submitted and can track status in eRA Commons. Fewer than three letters may render an application non-responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested content and selection of reference writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters should come from scientists who can address the PI’s ability to formulate a compelling scientific vision, record of overcoming conceptual/experimental hurdles, and capacity to challenge dogma. Avoid referees chosen primarily for official position or who could benefit from the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select referees who can credibly speak to creativity, impact, and independence; avoid collaborators or beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy (A1 not allowed) and referencing prior submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions (A1) are not allowed. Previously unfunded Pioneer applications may be submitted as 'new' applications, but applicants should not reference previous applications or reviews; references to prior submissions may result in administrative withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If re-submitting a prior idea, address reviewer comments in the new application but do not cite or attach prior reviews or application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process stages and interview format
rubrics_metrics.description: First stage: mail reviewers assess all applications. Second stage: separate panel of 12–15 distinguished scientists uses mail reviews to identify a subset invited to interview. Interviews consist of a 10-minute PI presentation followed by a 10-minute discussion. Panel members then score applications. Council of Councils conducts final review and NIH leadership makes funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a concise 10-minute presentation highlighting innovation, potential impact, and applicant vision; craft written essay for broadly knowledgeable reviewers rather than narrow specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criteria emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular emphasis will be given to the investigator's track record of creativity and impact, innovativeness of the research approaches, and the potential of the project to have a significant impact on an important research problem relevant to NIH. All standard review criteria will be weighed in determining the final impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize demonstrating creative track record and transformative potential; ensure the essay and reference letters highlight these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise and writing for non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no attempt to closely match reviewers’ expertise to proposal topics; reviewers are chosen for breadth and may not be experts in the specific topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the essay at a level appropriate for broadly knowledgeable scientists so non-experts can appreciate significance and innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No ability to suggest specific reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not name specific reviewers for their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include suggested reviewer names in the application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statements and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants will receive summary statements. Applicants not selected for interviews receive mail reviewer evaluations. Applicants selected to interview receive a resume and summary of discussion capturing outcomes of the interview along with mail reviewer critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use summary statements to inform future submissions but do not reference prior reviews in new Pioneer applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: No appeal process
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no appeal process for the outcome of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand decisions are final and plan next steps accordingly (e.g., submit a new application in a subsequent cycle if eligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award reporting and participation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients must submit an annual Research Performance Progress Report (2–5 pages), participate in the annual High-Risk, High-Reward Research Symposium, and may be contacted periodically for program evaluation for at least five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to provide concise annual reports and participate in program activities and evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public communication and acknowledgement of NIH support
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients should identify themselves as Pioneer Award recipients in journal articles, presentations, news releases, and other communications, and cite the grant number and program name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the example wording provided for acknowledgements and notify NIH of noteworthy publications or media coverage to be highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Public Access Policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by Federal legislation, NIH-funded scientists must submit final peer-reviewed journal manuscripts that arise from NIH funds to PubMed Central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH Public Access procedures for depositing accepted manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award non-renewability and transfer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Pioneer Awards are not renewable; awards can be transferred to another eligible U.S. institution per NIH policies but not to foreign institutions. Another investigator may assume PI responsibilities only to ramp down/close out the award (typically ~3 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan career moves and institutional arrangements mindful of transfer and non-renewal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional funds for Data Management and Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not request additional funds specifically for DMS; the Pioneer Award budget should accommodate data sharing within the fixed award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget data sharing and management within project planning without requesting extra direct costs.
